title: Transformers Don't Need LayerNorm at Inference Time: Implications for Interpretability
entrypoint: eval_pile.py (invocations listed in eval_all.sh reproduce the README table exactly)
primary_claim: LayerNorm can be removed from all GPT-2 models up to XL (1.5B parameters) via fine-tuning with only a small increase in cross-entropy loss (e.g. +0.0253 for XL), showing LN plays no substantial role in language modeling, though contrary to expectations attribution patching accuracy does not improve in LN-free models even as direct logit attribution becomes exact and entropy neurons stop functioning.
quote: Contrary to our expectations, we saw no improvement resulting from removing LayerNorm.
metric: cross-entropy loss increase, LN-free vs vanilla fine-tuned model, on The Pile-filtered
tolerance_rationale: headline is a compound of 4 numbers; compare the components by hand
blockers: Training new LN-free checkpoints from scratch needs 80GB+ GPU per README, but this is NOT required to reproduce the reported numbers since the exact checkpoints are already released on HF
python_version not pinned anywhere in the repo
inspector_notes: The paper's own headline CE-loss table is reproducible purely via inference on released HF checkpoints (eval_pile.py/eval_all.sh); the 80GB+ GPU requirement in the README applies only to re-deriving the LN-free checkpoints via training from scratch.
headline_artifact: README's cross-entropy loss table (OWT/Pile/Pile-filtered columns) for Small/Medium/Large/XL LN-free vs vanilla — matches target_value exactly
